Graph of a Fitted Parameter Against a Covariate

Source: R/plot_model.R
plot_param.Rd

Selects the graph of a parameter of the fitted distribution as a function of one covariate, on the scale of the parameter, with a pointwise confidence band. For a numeric covariate the parameter is drawn as a curve over the range of the covariate; for a factor, as one estimate with its interval per level.

Usage

plot_param(
  param,
  over,
  at = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov(),
  n_grid = 200,
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

param

The name of a parameter of the family, a single string.

over

The name of the covariate on the horizontal axis.

at

A named list of values for the other covariates, or NULL.

level

The confidence level of the band.

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance of the band.

n_grid

The number of points of the grid of a numeric covariate.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotParam object, inheriting from model_plot.

Details

The values are those of predict.StatmodFit() with what = param and se = TRUE on a grid of over. The other covariates are held at at, or at their median (numeric) or first level (factor), and the random effects are set to zero. The band is the interval of the parameter that predict.StatmodFit() returns for the variance selected by vcov_type, that is, the interval of the predictor mapped through the inverse link.

See also

autoplot.StatmodFit(), plot_quantiles(), plot_moments()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(150))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(150, sd = exp(-1 + dd$x))
fit <- statmod(y ~ x | sigma ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_param(param = "sigma", over = "x"),
                  data = dd)
